Alright, so just letting you know upfront I'm a few years too young to get a permit right now. However both my parents carry and I personally have competed in multiple pistol marksmanship tournaments and I've completed a course on home defense (Basically clearing rooms, making sure family is safe and that you are safe before countering a threat) so I'll try to give you my two cents.

Basically if you are not worried about brand I would consider getting a Glock or Smith and Wesson. Both brands in my experience are very well made and designed and have amazing customer support when it is (rarely) needed. I know my dad carries a S&W MP 9mm compact which he loves. Unfortunately the pistol is rather small and light which leads to a lot of sway and jerking if you are not familiar with compact pistols. If your hands are large like mine then the pistol is even worse because your ring and pinky fingers will have almost no grip on the firearm unless you use the magazines with the grip extensions.

While my Dad's gun is 9mm S&W do offer a full size .45 M&P firearm which should meet your needs. Keep in mind that I have not shot the .45 M&P, however I'm recommending it due to the fact that my Dad's 9mm Compact has never failed him and it is a great gun when you get used to it.

Glocks on the other hand are my favorite competition pistol. My mother also carries a Glock 30 with her at all times, I just asked her what she thinks of it and she said "It's alright". So I guess that means its about average...? I'll have to shoot her gun some day.

Now I'm going to talk about 1911's because you asked that in your other post. I love 1911's, actually, my whole family does. However unless you get a 1911 specifically meant for concealed carry you are going to have an awful time. My dad used to carry a 1911 before he got his M&P and while the gun was a great shooter it was awful for its weight and size. It's even worse if you live in a hot and humid area. Really I would only recommend getting a 1911 if you plan on doing open carry or plan on leaving your gun in the car, which in my opinion defeats the purpose of getting a permit in the first place.

That's just my two cents but good luck on getting your permit!

PS: I would also look into CZ and Springfield like what @Fuster_Cluck said. Both manufacturers are great and I've never had problems with their customer support either.
